title: Odd symmetrization preserves parameters for a property
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $T$ be a randomized sign tester on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, and let $P$ be a property of $[-1,1]$-valued functions on that cube. Suppose $P(f)$ implies $P$ for the odd part $x\mapsto(f(x)-f(-x))/2$ of $f$, every coordinate dictator is accepted by $T$ with probability at least $\beta$, and every odd function $f$ with property $P$ is accepted by $T$ with probability at most $B$. Then every coordinate dictator is accepted by the odd-symmetrized tester with probability at least $\beta$, and every function with property $P$ is accepted by the odd-symmetrized tester with probability at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $T$ is a sign tester on the $n$-cube
$P$ is a property of bounded cube functions
$P(f)$ implies $P$ of the odd part of $f$
Every coordinate dictator has acceptance probability at least $\beta$ under $T$
Every odd bounded cube function with property $P$ has acceptance probability at most $B$
